This is a RydeTAXI trip charged on the meter, so excess distance feeds directly into the fare and the RD-2 metered-distance remedy applies: Σ unexempted extra_km × per-km rate [F1][F6][F9][RD-1][RD-2]. The trace settles that two off-route segments exist (F4 and F5) and that the per-km rate is $1.4099 (= $13.14 ÷ 9.3 km) [F6][F9][RD-2].

Segment F4 (14:10–14:13, +1.63 km) is exempt. The trace marks the RD-4(a) test ✓: an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 13:52 on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, only 30 m from the optimal route, i.e. on the replaced stretch and before the 14:10 segment start, with two lanes closed [F17][RD-4]. Orchard Road band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 corroborates this severe congestion [F14][RD-4]. Rider counsel's own concession of the general congestion is consistent [RD-4]. RD-3(b) is squarely against the driver: the rider named no location in F11, the driver chose the Beach Road store himself on his own written account in F13, and the stop point in F2 sits 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, so the extra_km on that segment is not exempted by 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way'.

We do not allege an unpublished add-on: our claim is that the metered distance component — $13.14 for 9.3 km in F9 — and the $7.58 excess-distance amount in F6 are inflated by the unexempted segments, which is exactly the RD-2 metered-distance remedy.

The driver's own fallback concedes $3.99 for F5 alone, but F4 is not exempt: F14's band covers only 14:00–14:10 and is merely corroborative under RD-4(b) while F17's incident does not displace the 14:10–14:13 excursion, so 1.63 + 2.83 = 4.46 km × $1.41/km = $6.29 stands.

We press no account flag on the rider's side against the driver's route history, so D8 is not contested; the only review we ask for rests on F20's existing upheld dispute together with a further supported deviation, and it is an ancillary action that never decides the finding itself.

Conceded as to the literal numbers — F1 (9.3 km vs 3.9 km) and F3 (26.5 min vs 8 min) are system records and I do not dispute them — but RD-1 requires the reviewer to audit each off-route segment separately rather than treat the aggregate as one violation, and both segments have agreed or traffic-justified explanations (F10, F11, F14, F17).

Chat #2 (F11, 14:02) precedes both off-route segments' starts (F4 starts 14:10, F5 starts 14:17), which is exactly the RD-5 'before you go' condition; the rider consented to the Cavenagh routing and then, in the same message, asked for a 7-Eleven stop, so the rider's own request is what directed the vehicle away from the Orchard/Bras Basah corridor.

The rider named no location but the driver's chosen store sits on the agreed Cavenagh/Beach Road side of the optimal route, so under RD-3(a) the store is on the line of the agreed rerouted route and the deviation is attributable to the rider's stop request rather than to a unilateral route change; the rider never objected at the store or after (F11, F12).

F5 (2.83 km extra, up to 1553 m off the optimal route) is the segment that contains the agreed Cavenagh routing plus the rider-requested 7-Eleven stop, so it is exempt either as an RD-5 pre-agreed reroute or as an RD-3(a) rider-directed stop; the rider's reading would make the driver liable for a stop the rider himself requested.

Segment F4 is not covered by a speed band alone: RD-4(a) is satisfied directly by the LTA DataMall incident at F17 (accident reported 13:52, only 30 m from the optimal route, two lanes closed on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road — inside the trip window and before the 14:10 segment start), with F14 (band 1, 0–9 km/h on Orchard Road 14:00–14:10) as corroboration under RD-4(b).

Agreed — the rider does not claim the $1.08 waiting charge (F7), and on RydeTAXI the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) is chargeable metered waiting time under RD-3(c), so that item stands; my client asks that the same RD-3(c) treatment be applied consistently to the stop's existence rather than charging it back as an unexempted detour.
